To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The sum- and the difference-frequency of the fundamental and the second-harmonic of a powerful pulsed dye laser, pumped by a Q-switched Nd:YAG-laser, generate intense VUV radiation tunable between 1200 and 2105 A in krypton and in xenon.

the sum- and difference- frequency mixing of the fundamental and second harmonic light from a pulsed dye laser excited by the fourth harmonic of an Nd:Yag laser in xenon and in krypton generates intense VUV light pulses in the wavelength region between 1100-2100 A.

intense, tunable, narrowband VUV radiation can be generated in the wavelength range from 1226 to 2100 A by nonresonantly mixing the fundamental and second-harmonic radiation of a pulsed narrowband dye laser system with a powerful infrared laser.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of VUV laser system based on sum- and difference frequency mixing of the fundamental and second harmonic radiation of a dye laser in krypton and/or xenon.
the generation of intense tunable VUV light pulses by nonresonance sum- and difference- frequency mixing in rare gases.
the development of a tunable narrowband VUV light source with high pulse energy and power.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sum- and difference-frequencies are the most powerful VUV sources available at present.
this method is a very promising and versatile source for the generation of tunable VUV light.

the VUV generation by sum- and difference- frequency mixing of a pulsed dye laser with a Nd:YAG-laser is the most efficient method for the generation of intense narrowband VUV radiation in a large spectral range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conversion process omega(L) + 2omega(U) = 2hnu(VUV) in krypton and in xenon provides tunable narrowband VUV radiation in the wavelength region of 1100-2100 A with high conversion efficiencies.
we are now able to produce intense coherent VUV radiation in the wavelength region between 1100 A and 2100A with a continuous tuning capability.
the sum- and difference- frequency mixing of a powerful narrow-band dye laser with the fundamental and the second harmonic of a Nd:YAG-laser is a powerful source of coherent tunable VUV-radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conversion efficiency is not limited by saturation effects.
the conversion process is nonresonant.
the VUV light is produced by the interaction of a powerful narrow band UV laser with noble gas atoms.
